## Skill 18: Redux

## Skill 19: Node.js

### Beginner — 20 Questions

Q1 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_001]
What is Node.js?

A. A frontend framework for React
B. A JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine
C. A database management system
D. A library for styling HTML

Correct Answer: B

Q2 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_002]
Which of the following command-line tools is used to manage packages in Node.js?

A. pip
B. apt
C. npm
D. brew

Correct Answer: C

Q3 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_003]
How do you start a Node.js REPL in your terminal?

A. type `start node`
B. type `node`
C. type `npm run`
D. type `javascript`

Correct Answer: B

Q4 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_004]
Which of these files is used to store project metadata and dependencies?

A. index.js
B. config.node
C. package.json
D. app.xml

Correct Answer: C

Q5 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_005]
Which keyword is used to include a module in Node.js (CommonJS syntax)?

A. import
B. include
C. require
D. get

Correct Answer: C

Q6 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_006]
What is the default scope of a variable defined in a Node.js file?

A. Global
B. Local to the module
C. Local to the function only
D. Public to all files

Correct Answer: B

Q7 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_007]
Which object represents the current module and contains information about it?

A. global
B. window
C. module
D. context

Correct Answer: C

Q8 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_008]
How do you execute a script file named `app.js` using Node.js?

A. `run app.js`
B. `node app.js`
C. `npm app.js`
D. `start app.js`

Correct Answer: B

Q9 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_009]
What does the `__dirname` variable represent in Node.js?

A. The name of the current file
B. The directory name of the current module
C. The root directory of the OS
D. The user's home folder

Correct Answer: B

Q10 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_010]
Which built-in module is used to handle file paths?

A. fs
B. path
C. url
D. os

Correct Answer: B

Q11 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_011]
How do you initialize a new Node.js project?

A. `npm start`
B. `node init`
C. `npm init`
D. `npm install`

Correct Answer: C

Q12 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_012]
Node.js is primarily ______-threaded.

A. Single
B. Multi
C. Double
D. Triple

Correct Answer: A

Q13 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_013]
Which global object allows you to interact with the current Node.js process?

A. system
B. thread
C. process
D. machine

Correct Answer: C

Q14 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_014]
What is the purpose of the `node_modules` folder?

A. To store your source code
B. To store downloaded third-party packages
C. To store logs
D. To store compiled binaries

Correct Answer: B

Q15 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_015]
Which function is used to output text to the terminal in Node.js?

A. print()
B. echo()
C. console.log()
D. System.out.println()

Correct Answer: C

Q16 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_016]
Which built-in module is used to create a basic HTTP server?

A. net
B. http
C. server
D. request

Correct Answer: B

Q17 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_017]
Which command installs a package and adds it to the dependencies in `package.json`?

A. `npm install <package-name>`
B. `npm get <package-name>`
C. `npm add <package-name>`
D. `npm save <package-name>`

Correct Answer: A

Q18 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_018]
What is the extension for Node.js files?

A. .node
B. .js
C. .npm
D. .nj

Correct Answer: B

Q19 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_019]
What does "V8" refer to in the context of Node.js?

A. A high-performance database
B. Google’s open-source high-performance JavaScript engine
C. The version number of Node.js
D. A specific networking protocol

Correct Answer: B

Q20 [NODEJS_BEGINNER_020]
How do you access command-line arguments passed to a Node.js script?

A. `process.argv`
B. `args[]`
C. `module.args`
D. `env.arguments`

Correct Answer: A

### Intermediate — 20 Questions

Q1 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_001]
What is the purpose of the `EventEmitter` class in Node.js?

A. To handle database connections
B. To handle and emit custom events
C. To manage multi-threading
D. To style the console output

Correct Answer: B

Q2 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_002]
Which method of the `fs` module is used to read a file asynchronously?

A. `fs.readFileSync`
B. `fs.readFile`
C. `fs.openFile`
D. `fs.load`

Correct Answer: B

Q3 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_003]
What is the "Event Loop" in Node.js?

A. A cycle that checks for virus updates
B. A mechanism that handles asynchronous callbacks in a non-blocking way
C. A loop that iterates over an array
D. A way to restart the server automatically

Correct Answer: B

Q4 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_004]
How do you export a function named `myFunc` from a module in CommonJS?

A. `export myFunc;`
B. `module.exports = { myFunc };`
C. `exports.default = myFunc;`
D. `return myFunc;`

Correct Answer: B

Q5 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_005]
What is the difference between `setImmediate()` and `process.nextTick()`?

A. `setImmediate()` runs before `process.nextTick()`
B. `process.nextTick()` runs at the end of the current phase; `setImmediate()` runs in the next check phase of the event loop
C. There is no difference
D. `process.nextTick()` is used for UI updates

Correct Answer: B

Q6 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_006]
What is a "Buffer" in Node.js?

A. A temporary storage area for data being moved from one place to another (binary data)
B. A way to delay code execution
C. A styling tool for HTML
D. A database cache

Q7 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_007]

A. callback(err, data)
B. async/await or .then()/.catch()
C. try/except
D. Using the event emitter only

Q8 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_008]

A. To make the code run faster
B. To convert a callback-based function into a promise-based one
C. To create a new promise
D. To delete a promise

Q9 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_009]

Q10 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_010]

A. fs
B. system

D. process

Q11 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_011]

D. `myEmitter.start(...)`

Q12 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_012]

Q13 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_013]

A. A situation where the computer runs out of memory

C. An error that cannot be fixed
D. A performance optimization technique

Q14 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_014]

Q17 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_017]

A. The process continues running

C. It is automatically logged and ignored

Q19 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_019]

Q20 [NODEJS_INTERMEDIATE_020]

B. It contains `process.nextTick` and `Promise` callbacks; it is processed after the current operation and before the next phase of the event loop.
C. it handles only file system tasks.

Q5 [NODEJS_ADVANCED_005]

Q7 [NODEJS_ADVANCED_007]

Q9 [NODEJS_ADVANCED_009]

Q10 [NODEJS_ADVANCED_010]

Q19 [NODEJS_ADVANCED_019]

### Advanced — 20 Questions

Q1 [EXPRESS_ADVANCED_001]

## Skill 48: GitHub Actions

### Beginner — 20 Questions

Q1 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_001]
What is GitHub Actions?

A. A tool to chat with other GitHub users
B. An automation platform that allows you to create workflows directly in your GitHub repository
C. A database service hosted by GitHub
D. A graphic design tool for repository logos

Correct Answer: B

Q2 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_002]
In which directory must workflow files be stored within a GitHub repository?

A. `.github/scripts/`
B. `.github/workflows/`
C. `config/actions/`
D. `workflows/`

Correct Answer: B

Q3 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_003]
Which file format is used to define GitHub Actions workflows?

A. JSON
B. XML
C. YAML
D. TOML

Correct Answer: C

Q4 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_004]
What is a "Workflow" in GitHub Actions?

A. The list of all contributors to a project
B. A configurable automated process made up of one or more jobs
C. A type of branch protection rule
D. The speed at which code is committed

Correct Answer: B

Q5 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_005]
Which keyword in the YAML file is used to specify the events that trigger a workflow?

A. trigger:
B. start:
C. on:
D. event:

Correct Answer: C

Q6 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_006]
What is a "Job" in GitHub Actions?

A. A payment received for contributing to open source
B. A set of steps in a workflow that execute on the same runner
C. A single line of code in a script
D. A specific version of a repository

Correct Answer: B

Q7 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_007]
What is a "Step" in GitHub Actions?

A. An individual task that can run commands or actions in a job
B. A level in the folder structure
C. A commit made to the main branch
D. A software version number

Correct Answer: A

Q8 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_008]
What is a "Runner"?

A. A person who manages the repository
B. A server that executes the jobs in a workflow
C. A type of networking cable
D. A fast database query

Correct Answer: B

Q9 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_009]
Which keyword is used to define the type of machine to run a job on (e.g., `ubuntu-latest`)?

A. machine:
B. runs-on:
C. host:
D. platform:

Correct Answer: B

Q10 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_010]
What is an "Action" in the context of GitHub Actions?

A. A keyboard shortcut
B. A reusable extension that can simplify your workflow (e.g., checking out code)
C. A pull request comment
D. A repository star

Correct Answer: B

Q11 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_011]

A. `import: action-name`
B. `uses: action-name@version`
C. `include: action-name`
D. `apply: action-name`

Q12 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_012]

B. `on: commit`
3. `on: upload`
D. `on: sync`

B. False

Q15 [GITHUB_ACTIONS_BEGINNER_015]

Q14 [UNIT_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_014]

Q5 [UNIT_TESTING_ADVANCED_005]

## Skill 58: Integration Testing

## Skill 59: API Testing

### Beginner — 20 Questions

Q1 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_001]
What is the primary objective of API testing?

A. To test the graphical user interface (GUI)
B. To verify that the application programming interface meets expectations for functionality, reliability, and security
C. To design the database schema
D. To check the website's CSS styling

Correct Answer: B

Q2 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_002]
Which HTTP method is typically used to retrieve data from a server?

A. POST
B. PUT
C. GET
D. DELETE

Correct Answer: C

Q3 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_003]
What does a "404 Not Found" status code indicate?

A. The server is down
B. The request was successful
C. The requested resource could not be found on the server
D. The user is unauthorized

Correct Answer: C

Q4 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_004]
Which of the following is a common format for API request and response bodies?

A. JPG
B. JSON
C. MP3
D. EXE

Correct Answer: B

Q5 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_005]
What is an "Endpoint" in the context of an API?

A. The last line of the code
B. A specific URL where an API can be accessed by a client
C. The power button of the server
D. A database table name

Correct Answer: B

Q6 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_006]
Which HTTP status code category represents a successful request?

A. 1xx
B. 2xx
C. 4xx
D. 5xx

Correct Answer: B

Q7 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_007]
What is the purpose of "Headers" in an HTTP request?

A. To display a title on the webpage
B. To provide additional metadata about the request, such as content type or authentication tokens
C. To store the main data payload
D. To define the font size of the response

Correct Answer: B

Q8 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_008]
Which tool is widely used for manual and automated API testing?

A. Photoshop
B. Postman
C. Excel
D. Microsoft Word

Correct Answer: B

Q9 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_009]
What does the "POST" method usually do?

A. Deletes a resource
B. Updates a resource partially
C. Creates a new resource on the server
D. Refreshes the browser

Correct Answer: C

Q10 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_010]
True or False: API testing requires a fully functional frontend user interface to be performed.

A. True
B. False

Correct Answer: B — False

Q11 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_011]
Which HTTP status code represents "Internal Server Error"?

A. 200
B. 400
C. 401
D. 500

Correct Answer: D

Q12 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_012]
What is a "Payload" in API testing?

A. The cost of using the API
B. The actual data sent in the request or response body
C. The speed of the network
D. The number of characters in the URL

Correct Answer: B

Q13 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_013]
Which method is used to delete a resource from a server?

A. REMOVE
B. DROP
C. DELETE
D. CLEAR

Correct Answer: C

Q14 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_014]
What is the difference between "Body" and "Query Parameters"?

A. Body is for GET; Query Params are for POST.
B. Query Parameters are part of the URL; Body is a separate data block in the request.
C. Body is only for images.
D. There is no difference.

Correct Answer: B

Q15 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_015]
Which HTTP status code indicates a "Bad Request" (e.g., malformed syntax)?

A. 201
B. 400
C. 403
D. 503

Correct Answer: B

Q16 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_016]
What does "CRUD" stand for in API development?

A. Copy, Read, Unite, Delete
B. Create, Read, Update, Delete
C. Connect, Receive, Upload, Download
D. Create, Run, Undo, Disconnect

Correct Answer: B

Q17 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_017]
Which character is used to separate the base URL from query parameters?

A. &
B. #
C. ?
D. /

Correct Answer: C

Q18 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_018]
What is "Authentication" in API testing?

A. Checking if the server is real
B. Verifying the identity of the user or application making the request
C. Formatting the JSON data
D. Compressing the file size

Correct Answer: B

Q19 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_019]
True or False: A "201 Created" status code is usually the result of a successful GET request.

A. True
B. False

Correct Answer: B — False (Usually the result of a POST request)

Q20 [API_TESTING_BEGINNER_020]
What is the primary format used by the "REST" architectural style?

A. XML only
B. JSON only
C. Typically JSON, but can support various formats
D. CSV

Correct Answer: C

### Intermediate — 20 Questions

Q1 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_001]
What is the difference between "PUT" and "PATCH"?

A. PUT is for fetching; PATCH is for creating.
B. PUT replaces the entire resource; PATCH applies a partial update.
C. PATCH is for deleting; PUT is for updating.
D. They are exactly the same.

Correct Answer: B

Q2 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_002]
Which HTTP status code signifies that the client is "Unauthorized" and needs to provide credentials?

A. 400
B. 401
C. 403
D. 405

Correct Answer: B

Q3 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_003]
What does a "JSON Schema Validation" test check?

A. The speed of the response
B. If the response structure and data types match a predefined blueprint
C. If the user's password is correct
D. The number of records in the database

Correct Answer: B

Q4 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_004]
In Postman, what are "Environment Variables" used for?

A. To change the computer's OS settings
B. To store dynamic values (like URLs or tokens) that can be reused across different requests
C. To encrypt the hard drive
D. To list the names of the QA team

Correct Answer: B

Q5 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_005]
What is the purpose of the "204 No Content" status code?

A. The request failed because there was no data
B. The request was successful, but there is no representation to return to the client (often after a DELETE or PUT)
C. The database is empty
D. The user logged out

Correct Answer: B

Q6 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_006]
What is "Bearer Token" authentication?

A. A token shaped like a bear
B. An access token sent in the Authorization header to grant access to a resource
C. A username and password combined
D. A type of physical security key

Correct Answer: B

Q7 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_007]
Which status code represents "Forbidden" (client is authenticated but doesn't have permission)?

A. 401
B. 403
C. 404
D. 422

Correct Answer: B

Q8 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_008]
What is a "Regression Test" for an API?

A. Testing a new feature
B. Re-running previous tests to ensure new changes haven't broken existing functionality
C. Testing with a very slow internet connection
D. Deleting the API code

Correct Answer: B

Q9 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_009]
What is the purpose of "Response Time" validation in API testing?

A. To check the time of day
B. To ensure the API responds within an acceptable performance threshold
C. To count how many users are online
D. To measure the length of the JSON string

Correct Answer: B

Q10 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_010]
Which character is used to separate multiple query parameters in a URL?

A. ?
B. &
C. |
D. ;

Correct Answer: B

Q11 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_011]
What is "API Functional Testing"?

A. Testing how many functions are in the code
B. Verifying that the API performs its intended tasks and handles data correctly
C. Testing the hardware of the server
D. Testing the UI buttons

Correct Answer: B

Q12 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_012]
How do you test an API's "Error Handling"?

A. By always sending valid data
B. By sending invalid or unexpected inputs to ensure the API returns the correct error status codes and messages
C. By restarting the server
D. By checking the CSS of the error page

Correct Answer: B

Q13 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_013]
What is "Data-Driven Testing" in the context of APIs?

A. Testing only during the daytime
B. Running the same API request multiple times using different sets of input data from an external file (like CSV or JSON)
C. Testing with no data
D. Manually typing data into a form

Correct Answer: B

Q14 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_014]
What is the "Accept" header used for in a request?

A. To accept the terms of service
B. To tell the server which content types the client is able to process (e.g., application/json)
C. To provide the user's name
D. To authorize a payment

Correct Answer: B

Q15 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_015]
Which status code category represents "Redirection"?

A. 2xx
B. 3xx
C. 4xx
D. 5xx

Correct Answer: B

Q16 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_016]
What is the purpose of a "Collection" in Postman?

A. To collect money from users
B. To group and organize related API requests for easier management and testing
C. To store images
D. To list database tables

Correct Answer: B

Q17 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_017]
What is "API Mocking"?

A. Making fun of a developer's API
B. Creating a simulated version of an API that returns predefined responses for testing purposes
C. Copying an API from another site
D. Encrypting the API endpoint

Correct Answer: B

Q18 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_018]
What does a "503 Service Unavailable" status code usually mean?

A. The URL is misspelled
B. The server is temporarily unable to handle the request, often due to maintenance or overloading
C. The user's account was deleted
D. The API is free of charge

Correct Answer: B

Q19 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_019]
In automated testing, what is an "Assertion"?

A. A comment for the developer
B. A validation step that compares the actual result with the expected result
C. A way to skip a test
D. The name of the test file

Correct Answer: B

Q20 [API_TESTING_INTERMEDIATE_020]
What is "Rate Limiting" and how is it tested?

A. Limiting the speed of the mouse; tested with a stopwatch.
B. Restricting the number of requests a user can make; tested by sending more requests than allowed and verifying a 429 status code.
C. Limiting the storage size of the database.
D. Limiting the number of developers on a project.

Correct Answer: B

### Advanced — 20 Questions

Q1 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_001]
What is "Idempotency" in API design and why is it important for testing?

A. It is the ability to run on any OS.
B. It means a request can be repeated multiple times without changing the result; important to verify that retries don't cause duplicate side effects.
C. It is the speed of the API.
D. It is the encryption level of the payload.

Correct Answer: B

Q2 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_002]
How do you perform "Security Testing" on an API (e.g., checking for SQL injection)?

A. By checking the font size of the responses
B. By injecting malicious strings into request parameters/body to see if the API handles them safely
C. By changing the background color of the UI
D. By calling the developer on the phone

Correct Answer: B

Q3 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_003]
What is "HATEOAS" and how does it affect API testing?

A. It is a type of database index.
B. Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State; testers must verify that the API provides links to navigate through resources dynamically.
C. It is a security protocol for Wi-Fi.
D. It stands for High Availability Testing.

Correct Answer: B

Q4 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_004]
What is "Contract Testing" (e.g., using Pact)?

A. Reading a legal contract for errors
B. Verifying that the consumer (client) and provider (server) agree on the structure of their interaction
C. Testing the terms of service of the website
D. Deleting an old API agreement

Correct Answer: B

Q5 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_005]
How does "OAuth 2.0" flow testing differ from simple API key testing?

A. It doesn't require a network.
B. It involves multiple steps, including obtaining an authorization code, exchanging it for a token, and managing token expiration/refresh.
C. It only works for mobile apps.
D. Simple API key testing is more secure.

Correct Answer: B

Q6 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_006]
What is "Performance/Load Testing" for an API?

A. Checking if the API looks pretty
B. Simulating a high volume of concurrent users/requests to measure how the API handles stress and its breaking point
C. Measuring the file size of the documentation
D. Counting the number of lines of code

Correct Answer: B

Q7 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_007]
What is an "Intermittent Failure" (Flaky Test) in an API test suite?

A. A test that always fails
B. A test that passes or fails inconsistently without code changes, often due to race conditions or environment issues
C. A test written in a different language
D. A test for a deleted endpoint

Correct Answer: B

Q8 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_008]
How can "Service Virtualization" help in complex API testing scenarios?

A. By making the code run in a virtual machine
B. By simulating the behavior of dependent services that are unavailable, slow, or expensive to use during testing
C. By deleting the database
D. By using a virtual reality headset

Correct Answer: B

Q9 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_009]
What is "API Fuzzing"?

A. Making the API response blurry
B. Providing random, malformed, or unexpected data as input to find security loopholes or crash vulnerabilities
C. Styling the API documentation with CSS
D. A type of automated backup

Correct Answer: B

Q10 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_010]
How do you test "Race Conditions" in an API?

A. Run a single request very fast.
B. Send multiple concurrent requests targeting the same resource to see if they conflict or cause data corruption.
C. By using a stopwatch.
D. Race conditions are only a frontend issue.

Correct Answer: B

Q11 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_011]
What is "Idempotency Key" testing?

A. Testing a physical key for a server room
B. Verifying that including a unique key in a request header prevents the server from processing a duplicate request
C. Testing the database primary key
D. Changing the API key every hour

Correct Answer: B

Q12 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_012]
What is the "N+1 Problem" in the context of API design and testing?

A. Having one more user than the server can handle
B. An inefficiency where a client must make one query for a list and N additional queries for details, which tests should identify
C. A mathematical error in a loop
D. A type of network latency

Correct Answer: B

Q13 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_013]
How do you implement "API Chaining" in an automated test?

A. By linking multiple servers with a chain
B. By taking the output of one API request (e.g., an ID) and using it as the input for a subsequent request
C. By repeating the same request 100 times
D. By writing code in a circular way

Correct Answer: B

Q14 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_014]
What is "Static Analysis" for an API?

A. Testing while the server is turned off
B. Analyzing the API's definition (e.g., OpenAPI spec) or source code for errors and standards compliance without executing it
C. Measuring the electricity usage
D. Counting the number of users

Q15 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_015]

A. Checking if the token looks like JSON

C. Encrypting the user's password in the payload
D. Deleting the token after one use

Q16 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_016]
What is "Penetration Testing" for an API?

A. Testing the physical server casing
B. A simulated cyberattack to evaluate the security of the API and its underlying infrastructure
C. Testing how deep the database folders go
D. Checking for syntax errors

Q17 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_017]
How do you test "Pagination" with cursors versus offsets?

A. Cursor-based testing focuses on opaque strings; Offset-based focuses on page numbers.
B. Cursors are for desktop only.
C. Offsets are faster for large datasets.
D. They are tested identically.

Q18 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_018]
What is "Inter-service Testing" in a microservices environment?

A. Testing the customer service department
B. Testing the communication and data integrity between two or more internal services
C. Testing the Wi-Fi signal between servers
D. Testing the server hardware

Q19 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_019]

A. Negotiating the price of a subscription
B. Verifying that the API correctly returns data in the format requested by the client's "Accept" header
C. Agreeing on a database schema

Correct Answer: B

Q20 [API_TESTING_ADVANCED_020]
What is the purpose of testing "Idempotency in POST requests" if POST is typically not idempotent?

A. Because POST should always be idempotent.

Q17 [DESIGN_PATTERNS_ADVANCED_017]

Correct Answer: B
